mutants.description: Start-up from S_OFF checks only the enable and none of the hard faults, relying on en being fault-gated
mutants.reason: With g_en high and OTP, UVLO, latch_state or latch_assert present, the FSM leaves S_OFF for S_SS, then is forced back, so state_out and ss_active toggle OFF/SS every other clock instead of staying in S_OFF.

mutants.description: S_OFF starts straight into S_RUN when SS_done is still high, skipping the re-ramp
mutants.reason: If SS_done is high when the converter is enabled from S_OFF, run_active rises and ss_active never does, so the soft-start ramp is skipped, violating the rule that every start re-ramps.

mutants.description: The power-stage enable is decoded from next_state instead of the registered state
mutants.reason: en rises one clock early on start from S_OFF (while state_out is still S_OFF) and drops one clock early on a window trip, so en no longer matches the registered state.

mutants.description: Telemetry state_out shows the next state instead of the present registered state
mutants.reason: On any transition state_out changes one clock before ss_active/run_active/hiccup_active, e.g. it reads S_SS while still in S_OFF when enable is applied.

mutants.description: run_active is decoded as 'power stage switching' and so is also high in S_SS
mutants.reason: During soft start run_active and ss_active are both high, instead of run_active being high only in S_RUN.

mutants.description: The gate-drive enable relies on the state alone for the hard faults, dropping the combinational fault gating
mutants.reason: When OTP, UVLO, latch_state or latch_assert asserts in S_SS or S_RUN, en stays high for one more clock until the FSM registers S_OFF, instead of dropping on the same clock.

mutants.description: ss_active is dropped as soon as the ramp reports done, a clock before the FSM leaves S_SS
mutants.reason: On the clock in S_SS where SS_done is high, ss_active is low while state_out is still S_SS; with SS_done held and window_trip_SS asserted, ss_active is low throughout S_SS.

mutants.description: An overcurrent window trip in S_RUN re-ramps straight into S_SS instead of first serving the S_HICCUP cool-down
mutants.reason: When window_trip asserts in S_RUN, the next state is S_SS. ss_active rises instead of hiccup_active, and en stays high, so the converter keeps switching with no cool-down.

mutants.description: At the end of the cool-down S_HICCUP returns to S_OFF and relies on S_OFF to restart, instead of retrying directly into S_SS
mutants.reason: After hiccup_done, state_out shows S_OFF for one clock and ss_active/en rise a clock late. hiccup_active falls without ss_active rising on the same edge.

mutants.description: hiccup_active is decoded from next_state, so it leads the registered S_HICCUP state by one clock
mutants.reason: hiccup_active rises on the same clock that window_trip or window_trip_SS asserts, while state_out still shows S_RUN or S_SS. It falls on the hiccup_done clock, a clock before the state leaves S_HICCUP.

mutants.description: run_active is taken as 'regulating and gate drive on', so the combinational fault gating of en also drops it
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, when OTP, UVLO, latch_state, latch_assert or loss of g_en asserts, run_active falls on the same clock. In the original it falls on the next clock, with state_out still showing S_RUN in between.

mutants.description: hiccup_active is decoded as 'power stage held off by the state', so it is also high in S_OFF
mutants.reason: Out of reset and whenever the FSM sits in S_OFF, hiccup_active is high although the state is not S_HICCUP. This starts the hiccup timer and strike counter while the converter is off.

mutants.description: The overcurrent window trips are treated as hard fault inputs in the combinational gating of en
mutants.reason: On the clock where window_trip (in S_RUN) or window_trip_SS (in S_SS) asserts, en goes low while the state is still S_RUN or S_SS. In the original, en stays high until S_HICCUP registers.

mutants.description: In S_RUN only the physical switch is checked for disable: a host disable over SPI gates en but does not send the FSM to S_OFF
mutants.reason: If spi_enable drops in S_RUN with en_SW high, en goes low but state stays S_RUN and run_active stays high. When spi_enable returns, en comes straight back at full duty without the S_SS re-ramp.

after: if (~en_SW | latch_state | OTP | UVLO | latch_assert) begin

mutants.reason: When fault_arbiter raises window_trip_SS on the same clock that soft_start raises SS_done, the FSM goes to S_RUN instead of S_HICCUP, so run_active rises and hiccup_active stays low, en stays high, and the cool-down is skipped.

mutants.description: In S_SS an overcurrent window trip outranks a hard fault, so a coincident shutdown is first sent through S_HICCUP
mutants.reason: If a hard fault (OTP, UVLO, latch, latch_assert or loss of enable) arrives on the same clock as window_trip_SS in S_SS, the FSM enters S_HICCUP instead of S_OFF. hiccup_active and state_out show S_HICCUP for a clock, and strike_counter counts a strike.

mutants.description: Start-up from S_OFF tests the gated gate-drive enable en instead of the combined converter enable g_en, confusing the output enable with the enable request
mutants.reason: In S_OFF en_from_state is 0 so en is always low, and the FSM never leaves S_OFF: with en_SW and spi_enable high and no fault, ss_active, en and state_out stay at S_OFF instead of starting soft start.

mutants.description: The disable test in S_HICCUP uses the gated gate-drive enable en instead of the converter enable g_en, so the cool-down's own gate-drive-off reads as a disable
mutants.reason: en is always low in S_HICCUP, so after a window trip the FSM leaves for S_OFF one clock after entering S_HICCUP, then restarts into S_SS without waiting for hiccup_done: hiccup_active lasts one clock and the cool-down is skipped.
before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
after: if (~en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin

mutants.description: ss_active is decoded as 'ramping with the gate drive on', so the combinational fault gating of en also drops it before the FSM leaves S_SS
mutants.reason: When a hard fault or disable arrives during soft start, ss_active falls on the same clock as en instead of a clock later when the FSM registers S_OFF. The ramp and the soft-start overcurrent window are therefore cleared one clock early.

mutants.description: hiccup_active is decoded as 'cool-down still running', so a hard fault or disable drops it combinationally before the FSM leaves S_HICCUP
mutants.reason: When OTP, UVLO, the latch or a disable arrives during the cool-down, hiccup_active falls on that clock instead of a clock later with the registered move to S_OFF. The hiccup timer and strike counter are therefore released early.

mutants.description: Every start from S_OFF goes through the S_HICCUP cool-down before soft start, as if each restart after a shutdown needed the same off-time as a fault retry
mutants.reason: When the converter is enabled with no fault present, en stays low and hiccup_active goes high for a whole cool-down interval before S_SS and the gate drive begin. On every start the strike counter also sees S_HICCUP entered.

mutants.description: Telemetry state_out reports S_RUN as soon as the ramp reports SS_done, instead of the registered present state
mutants.reason: On the clock SS_done rises in S_SS, state_out reads S_RUN a clock before the FSM registers S_RUN. If window_trip_SS fires on that same clock, state_out shows S_RUN while the FSM goes from S_SS to S_HICCUP.

mutants.description: The combined converter enable g_en is registered instead of combinational, so the switch and host enables reach the gate drive and the FSM a clock late
mutants.reason: If en_SW or spi_enable falls in S_SS or S_RUN, en stays high for one more clock and the FSM registers S_OFF a clock late. A start from S_OFF also moves to S_SS a clock after the enable rises.
before: Combine the two enables. The physical switch and the host must both allow the
converter to run; either one alone turns it off.
after: Combine the two enables. The physical switch and the host must both allow the
converter to run; either one alone turns it off.

mutants.description: The LM5106 enable en is registered to give a glitch-free gate drive, so it follows the state and the fault inputs one clock late
mutants.reason: en rises one clock after the FSM registers S_SS. It stays high for one clock after S_RUN gives way to S_HICCUP on window_trip. After OTP, UVLO, latch_state, latch_assert or a disable, it drops a clock late instead of on the same clock.
before: Drive the LM5106 enable. Gated by the fault inputs directly as well as by the
state, so a trip pulls the gate drive low combinationally, on the same clock,
instead of a clock later when the FSM has registered S_OFF.
after: Drive the LM5106 enable. Gated by the fault inputs directly as well as by the
state, so a trip pulls the gate drive low combinationally, on the same clock,
instead of a clock later when the FSM has registered S_OFF.

withdrawn.description: The host enable over SPI is treated as a start request checked only in S_OFF, so a host disable while ramping, running or in hiccup is ignored
withdrawn.reason: If spi_enable falls while the FSM is in S_SS or S_RUN with en_SW high, the original drops en at once and goes to S_OFF; the mutant keeps en high and stays in its state until the physical switch or a fault turns it off.
withdrawn.withdrawn: the per-state enable mutants combined: a host (AIM.41) or switch (AIM.76) disable ignored in S_SS, S_RUN and S_HICCUP gives the same wrong state as AIM.46/15/47 or AIM.55/50/56, so any test that kills one of those kills it

withdrawn.description: The physical switch en_SW is treated as a start request checked only in S_OFF, so turning it off while ramping, running or in hiccup is ignored
withdrawn.reason: In S_SS, S_RUN or S_HICCUP, turning en_SW low no longer pulls en low or sends the FSM to S_OFF. The converter keeps switching, and a hiccup retries into S_SS, until the host disables it over SPI or a hard fault occurs.

withdrawn.description: S_HICCUP has no hard-fault exit: the designer relied on the gate drive already being off and only waits for hiccup_done
withdrawn.reason: A hard fault or loss of g_en during the cool-down leaves the FSM in S_HICCUP (hiccup_active high, state_out = S_HICCUP) until hiccup_done, then it goes to S_SS, instead of going to S_OFF at once.
